title: A Fair Bayesian Inference through Matched Gibbs Posterior
topic: Social Aspects->Fairness, Equity, Justice and Safety
claim: Our method achieves a better fairness–utility and fairness–uncertainty Pareto frontier than competing fair-learning baselines across several metrics.
layout: 4 panels in a row, shared x-axis, metric-specific y-axes, shared legend
description: A row of four line-and-scatter plots, labeled (a) CRIME-Acc, (b) CRIME-Nll, (c) CRIME-brier and (d) CRIME-Ece. Each panel puts the fairness deviation Δ_W^{1/2} on the x-axis, from 0 to 0.6. The y-axes are accuracy, NLL, Brier score and ECE. Six methods appear as colored Pareto-front curves with error bars: gapreg, reduction, variational_mmd, adv, gibbs_mmd and gibbs_matched, the last marked with a check mark and drawn in lime green. A legend sits inside each panel. The gray adv curve has large error bars and is the clear outlier. The green gibbs_matched curve is visibly better, with higher accuracy and lower NLL and Brier than the others. The eye goes to the green curve first, since it separates from the cluster of other lines.

abstract: With the growing importance of trustworthy AI, algorithmic fairness has emerged as a critical concern. Among various fairness notions, group fairness - which measures the model bias between sensitive groups - has received significant attention. While many group-fair models have focused on satisfying group fairness constraints, model uncertainty has received relatively little attention, despite its importance for robust and trustworthy decision-making. To address this, we adopt a Bayesian framework to capture model uncertainty in fair model training. We first define group-fair posterior distributions and then introduce a fair variational Bayesian inference. Then we propose a novel distribution termed matched Gibbs posterior, as a proxy distribution for the fair variational Bayesian inference by employing a new group fairness measure, the matched deviation. A notable feature of matched Gibbs posterior is that it approximates the posterior distribution well under the fairness constraint without requiring heavy computation. Theoretically, we show that the matched deviation has a strong relation to existing group fairness measures, highlighting desirable fairness guarantees. Computationally, by treating the matching function in the matched deviation as a learnable parameter, we develop an efficient MCMC algorithm. Experiments on real-world datasets demonstrates that matched Gibbs posterior outperforms other methods in balancing uncertainty–fairness and utility–fairness trade-offs, while also offering additional desirable properties.
